objective: Make every main thread that loads the holyagent plugin receive the root rules even when the SessionStart hook output arrives late or never, so the holyagent way is the default with no user nudge.
scope: Evidence from session_012tBKnb2s5Pj2Z6LXoSmUTW (claude.ai web, default cloud environment, no repository): the main thread ran as the default agent for its first 13 actions; holyagent 0.1.2-3 loaded and its CLI worked; no SessionStart hook output is in the feed; the init event shows hooks_init_ms 47165 and new_plugin_hooks_join_ms 81167, so the synced plugin's hooks joined after the first prompt (13:42:51) and the plugin settings.json agent key did not make the main thread the root. Design: deliver the root core rules (the same text session-start injects: ROOT_CORE plus the takeover line and the absolute CLI form) on the first main-thread hook event of a session that has not received them yet: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse (any tool, main thread only: skip when the payload carries an agent_id/agent_type of a subagent or when agent_type is holyagent). Record per session_id that the rules were delivered, in a small marker outside the repository (for example under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} or os.tmpdir()/holyagent-sessions/<session_id>), so each session gets them once; also re-deliver after compaction (SessionStart source compact) as today. UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse return the text as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. Add a UserPromptSubmit hook to hooks.json in packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts and extend the existing PreToolUse entry (or add a catch-all one) without changing what the existing PreToolUse hooks already do.
Make failures visible to the model where possible: if session-start fails, emit a short context line saying the holyagent rules could not load and where to read them, instead of exiting with nothing.

Tests: a session whose first hook is UserPromptSubmit gets the rules once; a later PreToolUse in the same session gets nothing extra; a subagent PreToolUse gets nothing; SessionStart then UserPromptSubmit delivers once; compaction re-delivers. Update docs/hooks.md.

notes:
- **Design choices.**
  - The new `root-rules` hook is wired to UserPromptSubmit and to PreToolUse with no matcher. The PreToolUse entry is appended after the existing ones, which are unchanged.
  - It adds `bareContext(core, cloud)`, the same text session-start gives a project with no state.
  - It is silent for the root, for a subagent (payload has `agent_id`, or an `agent_type` that is a plugin specialist), for events other than those two, and for a missing or unsafe `session_id`.
  - Delivery is claimed with an exclusive-create marker at `os.tmpdir()/holyagent-sessions/<session_id>`. Parallel tool calls cannot both win; a test with six racing calls proves it.
  - SessionStart still always delivers as before, and writes the marker (best effort) when it delivers the core. A compact re-delivers.
- **SessionStart failure.** For a main thread that is not the root, session-start no longer exits 1 with nothing. It emits the core rules plus one line naming the failure tag and `holyagent status`, with exit 0. The root keeps the existing exit 1 with a stderr line, because the host reads nothing from a failed hook and the root has its rules in the prompt; this keeps the existing tests unchanged. The line says the project state could not be read, not that the rules could not load, because the rules still load in that case.
- **Marker write failure.** In `root-rules` this is exit 1 with a stderr line and no delivery, so a broken marker folder never causes a delivery on every tool call.
- **Cost.** The hook starts Bun on every main-thread tool call, even though it prints nothing after the first delivery. The cost is documented in `docs/hooks.md`.
- **Unrun.** I did not run this against a live claude.ai session.
